title: lint: judge beforeInsert created_at / updated_at by hook priority (only a hook below 10 reads them null)
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQjrEpxMVxEiDUJHqC

Follow-up from PR #34129 (card #33435): r1 S2 (record 6901107947), r3 N5 (record 6903617482), and seat ruling 6901005939.

**Now.** `validate-expressions.ts` refuses an unguarded ordering or arithmetic over `record.created_at` / `record.updated_at` in the `condition` of every hook whose `events` include `beforeInsert`, whatever the hook's `priority`. Hooks run in ascending `priority`, the stamp sits at 10, and `HookSchema.priority` defaults to 100. So only a hook authored below 10 reads null. Every hook at the default priority is refused although it can never meet null. #34129 scoped the prose to "priority below 10"; the rule itself did not change.

**Ask.**
1. Read `hook.priority` (default 100) at both doors, `os build` and the publish gate, and add `created_at` / `updated_at` to the nullable index only when priority < 10.
2. Pin it with three hooks: priority 5 refused; default priority accepted; priority 10 at the boundary, judged against where the stamp hook actually runs, with the reading written into the test.
3. Fix the `flows.mdx` rule 5 sentence (r3 N5). It says `created_at` / `updated_at` "need none", but the publish gate drops only the *ordering* finding on those two columns. Arithmetic on `record.created_at`, and a `previous.created_at` read, are still refused there without the guard. Either narrow the sentence to comparisons, or close that residue in the same change.

This is a widening, so it needs `Clause-②` and an ADR-0087 entry for the accept-set change.
